title: Setting the Boundaries of AI
subject: AI-Literacy
description: Comprehensive practice on how humans guide, instruct, train and correct AI — covering the human-to-AI pipeline, human vs AI roles, human judgement versus AI patterns, everyday examples of AI automation, the AI villain game, AI safety, fixing AI mistakes, and the real-world Google/ImageNet story of training AI with human-labelled data.

questions.question: According to this chapter, what is the FIRST step that leads to an AI being built?
options: A Human Idea
An AI Output
A Robot
A Computer Chip
questions.explanation: Every AI starts with a human idea — someone imagines what they want the AI to do, before any programming or training happens.

questions.question: In the chain 'Human Idea → ___ → ___ → AI Output', what is the LAST step?
options: AI Output
Human Idea
Training
Instructions
questions.explanation: The chain ends with AI Output — the result the AI produces after being given instructions and trained with data.

questions.question: What word from the chapter's word bank means the written rules a human gives to the AI?
options: Instructions
Colour
Weather
Song
questions.explanation: 'Instructions' are the rules humans write to tell the AI what to do.

questions.question: Humans give AI instructions before it can be trained.
questions.explanation: In the chain, Instructions come before Training — humans set the rules first, then the AI is trained using data.

questions.question: Which word describes how an AI learns to react using lots of examples?
options: Training
Painting
Singing
Sleeping
questions.explanation: Training is the process where an AI learns from lots of examples (data) how to react.

questions.question: Training an AI mainly involves giving it lots of ____.
options: Data
Toys
Music
Paint
questions.explanation: Training uses lots of data so the AI can learn patterns and react correctly.

questions.question: Which order correctly leads to an AI Output?
options: Human Idea → Instructions → Data/Training
Instructions → Human Idea → Data/Training
Data/Training → Human Idea → Instructions
Human Idea → Data/Training → Instructions
questions.explanation: A human first has the idea, then writes instructions, and only then is the AI trained with data before producing output.

questions.question: Which of these correctly fills BOTH blanks: 'Human Idea → ___ → ___ → AI Output'?
options: Instructions, Training
AI Output, Human Idea
Robot, Game
Mistake, Fix
questions.explanation: The chain goes Human Idea → Instructions → Training → AI Output.

questions.question: Select ALL the words that come from the chapter's word bank for completing the AI chain.
options: Instructions
Training
Data
Program
Robot
questions.explanation: The word bank for this activity is Instructions, Training, Data and Program. 'Robot' is not part of it.

questions.question: Why does the chain start with a 'Human Idea' and not an 'AI Idea'?
options: Because AI cannot think of what it should do on its own; a human must decide
Because AI is faster at having ideas
Because computers do not need ideas
Because the idea does not matter
questions.explanation: AI cannot imagine a purpose for itself — a human must first decide what the AI is for.

questions.question: In this chapter's chain, 'Training' happens before 'Instructions' are given.
questions.explanation: Instructions come first, setting the rules; Training with data happens after, so the AI can learn to follow those rules.

questions.question: The word 'Program' in the word bank is closest in meaning to which other word in the same word bank?
options: Instructions
Training
Data
AI Output
questions.explanation: 'Program' and 'Instructions' both describe the rules humans write to tell the AI what to do.

questions.question: The word 'Data' in the word bank is closest in meaning to which other word in the same word bank?
options: Training
Instructions
Human Idea
AI Output
questions.explanation: Data is what an AI uses during Training to learn how to react.

questions.question: What does 'AI Output' mean?
options: The result or answer the AI produces
The idea a human has
The data used for training
The rules written by a programmer
questions.explanation: AI Output is the final result the AI produces after being trained.

questions.question: 'AI Output' comes at the very end of the chain, after training.
questions.explanation: The chain ends with AI Output, which comes after the AI has been trained.

questions.question: A classmate says: 'AI has ideas all by itself, without any human.' What is wrong with this statement, based on the chapter's chain?
options: The chain always starts with a Human Idea, not an AI idea
AI never produces any output
Training never uses data
Humans are not involved anywhere in the chain
questions.explanation: The chapter's chain always begins with a Human Idea — AI does not invent its own purpose.

questions.question: According to the chain in this chapter, an AI Output can appear without ever starting from a Human Idea.
questions.explanation: Every AI Output in this chain traces back to a Human Idea that started the whole process.

questions.question: Which statement best matches the chapter's message about the AI chain?
options: Every AI Output can be traced back to a human idea and human-given instructions
AI Output always comes before Human Idea
Training happens without any data
Instructions are not needed once training starts
questions.explanation: The chapter shows AI Output depends on the earlier human-led steps of idea, instructions and training.

questions.question: Instructions given to an AI are also sometimes called a ____ in the chapter's word bank.
options: Program
Song
Sport
Weather
questions.explanation: 'Program' is another word bank term closely linked to Instructions.

questions.question: What do humans use to train an AI so it can react properly?
options: Data
Candles
Bricks
Paint
questions.explanation: Data is used during training so the AI can learn how to react.

questions.question: Select ALL the steps that happen BEFORE 'AI Output' in the chapter's chain.
options: Human Idea
Instructions
Training
Fixing mistakes after release
questions.explanation: Human Idea, Instructions and Training all come before AI Output. Fixing mistakes after release happens after the AI is already producing output.

questions.question: The chapter's chain shows that AI needs both instructions and training data to work.
questions.explanation: The chain includes both Instructions and Training (with Data) as steps before AI Output.

questions.question: If a step is missing from the chain 'Human Idea → Instructions → Training → AI Output', which part is most likely to go wrong?
options: The final AI Output, since it depends on all earlier human-guided steps
Nothing changes
Only the colour of the output changes
The chain repeats itself automatically
questions.explanation: Since each step builds on the one before, skipping a step would affect the final AI Output.

questions.question: Why is 'Human Idea' placed BEFORE 'Instructions' in the chain, and not after?
options: Because you must first decide WHAT you want before you can write instructions for HOW to do it
Because instructions must always come first
Because AI writes its own idea after training
Because the order does not matter at all
questions.explanation: You need an idea first to know what instructions to write — the 'what' comes before the 'how'.

questions.topic: Who's in Control: Human or AI?
questions.question: Who usually chooses WHAT DATA should be used to train an AI?
options: A human
The AI itself
Nobody decides this
The screen
questions.explanation: Choosing the training data is a human job, done before the AI learns anything.

questions.topic: Who's in Control: Human or AI?
questions.question: Who or what FOLLOWS the programmed rules once an AI is running?
options: The AI
A human teacher
A parent
Nobody
questions.explanation: Once programmed, the AI is the one that follows the rules automatically.

questions.topic: Who's in Control: Human or AI?
questions.question: Who usually FIXES MISTAKES in an AI system?
options: A human
The AI itself
The screen
Nobody
questions.explanation: Fixing mistakes is a human responsibility, since AI cannot judge or correct its own errors.

questions.topic: Who's in Control: Human or AI?
questions.question: What SHOWS the results of an AI's work on a screen?
options: The AI/program
A human directly
A pencil
A book
questions.explanation: Displaying results on a screen is something the AI/program does automatically.

questions.topic: Who's in Control: Human or AI?
questions.question: Select ALL the actions in this chapter that are done by a HUMAN, not the AI.
options: Choosing what data should be used
Following programmed rules
Fixing mistakes in the system
Showing results on a screen
questions.explanation: Choosing training data and fixing mistakes are human tasks. Following rules and showing results are done by the AI.

questions.topic: Who's in Control: Human or AI?
questions.question: Select ALL the actions in this chapter that are done by the AI, not a human.
options: Following programmed rules
Choosing what data should be used
Showing results on a screen
Fixing mistakes in the system
questions.explanation: Following programmed rules and showing results on a screen are AI tasks. Choosing data and fixing mistakes are human tasks.

questions.topic: Who's in Control: Human or AI?
questions.question: Choosing what data an AI should be trained on is a HUMAN job.
questions.explanation: Humans decide what data will be used to train an AI.

questions.topic: Who's in Control: Human or AI?
questions.question: Following programmed rules is something the AI does automatically.
questions.explanation: Once instructions are set, the AI follows them automatically.

questions.topic: Who's in Control: Human or AI?
questions.question: Fixing mistakes in an AI system is normally done by the AI itself, without any human.
questions.explanation: This is a common misconception — fixing mistakes is a HUMAN job, since AI cannot reliably recognise or take responsibility for its own errors.

questions.topic: Who's in Control: Human or AI?
questions.question: Why is 'choosing what data should be used' a human job and not an AI job?
options: Because the AI has not learned anything yet before training data is chosen
Because AI always chooses its own data
Because data does not matter for training
Because only computers can pick data
questions.explanation: Before training begins, there is no AI 'judgement' yet, so a human must decide the data.

questions.topic: Who's in Control: Human or AI?
questions.question: Why is 'fixing mistakes in the system' listed as a human task?
options: Because AI cannot recognise or take responsibility for its own errors
Because AI never makes mistakes
Because mistakes fix themselves automatically
Because only screens can show mistakes
questions.explanation: AI does not truly understand when it is wrong or why, so a human must step in to fix errors.

questions.topic: Who's in Control: Human or AI?
questions.question: A friend says: 'The AI decides what data trains it, so no human is needed there.' What is wrong with this claim?
options: Humans are the ones who choose the training data, not the AI
AI never uses data
Training data does not exist
This statement is correct
questions.explanation: Choosing training data is a human decision, made before the AI has learned anything.

questions.topic: Who's in Control: Human or AI?
questions.question: Since an AI can display results on a screen by itself, no human decision was involved anywhere in the process.
questions.explanation: Even though showing results is automatic, humans still made earlier decisions, like choosing the data and writing the instructions.

questions.topic: Who's in Control: Human or AI?
questions.question: Which of these is something the AI itself does automatically, once it is trained?
options: Follow its programmed rules
Decide which data to use for training
Fix its own mistakes without any help
Choose the goal of the project
questions.explanation: Once trained, the AI automatically follows the rules it was given.

questions.topic: Who's in Control: Human or AI?
questions.question: Which of these is something ONLY a human can do, according to this chapter?
options: Decide what data to use for training
Show text on a screen
Follow a rule that is already programmed
Repeat a pattern
questions.explanation: Deciding the training data is a human responsibility in this chapter's activity.

questions.topic: Who's in Control: Human or AI?
questions.question: What is the main difference between 'following programmed rules' and 'fixing mistakes in the system'?
options: Following rules is what the AI does automatically; fixing mistakes needs human judgement
Both are done only by AI
Both are done only by humans
There is no difference
questions.explanation: The AI follows rules automatically, but correcting errors requires human judgement.

questions.topic: Who's in Control: Human or AI?
questions.question: Select ALL the roles that show HUMANS are in control of an AI system.
options: Choosing training data
Fixing mistakes
The AI showing an answer on a screen
The AI following its rules
questions.explanation: Choosing training data and fixing mistakes both show human control. The other two are automatic AI actions.

questions.topic: Who's in Control: Human or AI?
questions.question: If an AI gives a wrong answer, who is responsible for correcting it?
options: A human
The screen
The data itself
Nobody
questions.explanation: Humans are responsible for correcting an AI's mistakes.

questions.topic: Who's in Control: Human or AI?
questions.question: An AI 'showing results on a screen' means the AI is displaying what it has already computed.
questions.explanation: Showing results is the AI simply displaying the output it has produced.

questions.topic: Who's in Control: Human or AI?
questions.question: Which pair correctly matches a HUMAN task with an AI task?
options: Human: choosing data | AI: following rules
Human: following rules | AI: choosing data
Human: showing results | AI: fixing mistakes
Both tasks belong to the AI
questions.explanation: Humans choose the data; the AI follows the rules it was given.

questions.topic: Who's in Control: Human or AI?
questions.question: Which of these four tasks is the ODD ONE OUT because it is done by the AI, not a human?
options: Following programmed rules
Choosing what data should be used
Fixing mistakes in the system
None — humans do all four
questions.explanation: Following programmed rules is the AI's job, while the other listed tasks are human jobs.

questions.topic: Who's in Control: Human or AI?
questions.question: In this chapter, which word best matches 'AI' when sorting H (human) or AI tasks?
options: Following rules and showing results
Choosing data and fixing mistakes
Only fixing mistakes
Only choosing data
questions.explanation: Following programmed rules and showing results are the AI's automatic tasks.

questions.topic: Who's in Control: Human or AI?
questions.question: In this chapter, which word best matches 'H' (human) when sorting H or AI tasks?
options: Choosing data and fixing mistakes
Following rules and showing results
Only following rules
Only showing results
questions.explanation: Choosing training data and fixing mistakes are the human's tasks.

questions.topic: Who's in Control: Human or AI?
questions.question: According to this chapter, an AI can choose its own training data without any human decision.
questions.explanation: Choosing training data is described as a human job in this chapter's activity.

questions.topic: Who's in Control: Human or AI?
questions.question: Select ALL the reasons humans stay in control of an AI system.
options: Humans decide what data trains it
Humans fix its mistakes
The AI decides everything by itself
The AI never needs any human input
questions.explanation: Humans stay in control by choosing training data and fixing mistakes — the other two options are false.

questions.topic: Who's in Control: Human or AI?
questions.question: What is the purpose of sorting tasks into 'H' (human) and 'AI' in this chapter's activity?
options: To show where humans guide AI and where AI acts on its own
To test typing speed
To colour a picture
To count numbers
questions.explanation: The sorting activity helps students see which jobs need a human and which the AI does automatically.

questions.topic: Building an AI Game Step by Step
questions.question: What is the FIRST step when game creators build a video game with AI characters?
options: Deciding what the game is about and how it will be played
Testing the finished game
Fixing bugs
Giving the game lots of data
questions.explanation: Game creators start by thinking of the idea — what the game is about and how players will play it.

questions.topic: Building an AI Game Step by Step
questions.question: What do game creators do right after deciding the idea for the game?
options: Write computer code to control the characters and actions
Fix mistakes
Test the game with friends
Sell the game
questions.explanation: After the idea, game creators write the code that controls the characters and their actions.

questions.topic: Building an AI Game Step by Step
questions.question: After writing the code, what do game creators give the game so characters can learn to react?
options: Lots of data
A new idea
A different game
Nothing else is needed
questions.explanation: Game creators give the game lots of data so the characters can learn how to react.

questions.topic: Building an AI Game Step by Step
questions.question: What is the step that checks if the game is fun and works properly?
options: Testing
Coding
Idea
Data collection
questions.explanation: Testing is when game creators check that the game is fun and works properly.

questions.topic: Building an AI Game Step by Step
questions.question: What is the LAST step in building the game, according to this chapter?
options: Fixing mistakes and updating the game
Thinking of the idea
Giving data
Writing the code
questions.explanation: The final step is fixing mistakes and updating the game to make it better.

questions.topic: Building an AI Game Step by Step
questions.question: Put these steps in the correct order: (i) Test the game (ii) Think of the idea (iii) Give the game data (iv) Write the code (v) Fix mistakes
options: ii, iv, iii, i, v
i, ii, iii, iv, v
v, iv, iii, ii, i
ii, iii, iv, i, v
questions.explanation: The correct order is: idea, code, data, test, then fix mistakes.

questions.topic: Building an AI Game Step by Step
questions.question: Which step comes BETWEEN writing the code and testing the game?
options: Giving the game lots of data so characters can learn to react
Thinking of the idea
Selling the game
Nothing comes between them
questions.explanation: After coding, the game is given data to train its characters, and only then is it tested.

questions.topic: Building an AI Game Step by Step
questions.question: Why must 'writing the code' happen BEFORE 'giving the game data'?
options: The code sets up the rules the characters follow, and data teaches them how to react within those rules
Data always comes before any coding
Testing must happen first
The order does not matter
questions.explanation: The code creates the rules first; then data trains characters to react correctly within those rules.

questions.topic: Building an AI Game Step by Step
questions.question: Why does 'testing the game' come AFTER giving it data, not before?
options: You need the trained characters and code in place before you can check if the finished game works properly
Testing always happens first in every project
Data is not needed for testing
Fixing mistakes always happens before testing
questions.explanation: Testing checks the finished, trained game — so code and data must already be in place.

questions.topic: Building an AI Game Step by Step
questions.question: Select ALL the steps that happen AFTER the game creators have an idea.
options: Writing the code
Giving the game data
Testing the game
Having the idea itself
questions.explanation: Writing the code, giving data and testing all happen after the initial idea.

questions.topic: Building an AI Game Step by Step
questions.question: Game creators think of the game's idea before they write any code.
questions.explanation: The idea always comes first, before any code is written.

questions.topic: Building an AI Game Step by Step
questions.question: Testing a game happens before any code is written.
questions.explanation: This is backwards — code must be written and the game trained with data before it can be tested.

questions.topic: Building an AI Game Step by Step
questions.question: Fixing mistakes and updating the game is the very last step in this process.
questions.explanation: Fixing mistakes and updating the game comes after testing, as the final step.

questions.topic: Building an AI Game Step by Step
questions.question: A student says: 'Game creators give the game data before deciding what the game is about.' What is wrong with this?
options: The idea always comes first — data cannot be collected for a game that has not been imagined yet
Data always comes before the idea
There is no idea step in game creation
This statement is correct
questions.explanation: You must first decide what the game is about before you know what data the characters need.

questions.topic: Building an AI Game Step by Step
questions.question: According to the chapter, the 5 steps of building this game are proof that humans lead AI creation from start to finish.
questions.explanation: All five steps (idea, code, data, test, fix) are done or led by human game creators.

questions.topic: Building an AI Game Step by Step
questions.question: Why does this video game example help explain the AI chain from earlier in the chapter?
options: It shows the same idea -> instructions/code -> data/training -> output pattern in a real, human-led project
It has nothing to do with the AI chain
It shows AI can build games without any humans
It replaces the need for testing
questions.explanation: The 5 game-building steps mirror the earlier idea/instructions/training/output chain.

questions.topic: Building an AI Game Step by Step
questions.question: What do game characters use 'lots of data' for, according to this chapter?
options: Learning how to react
Changing colour
Nothing at all
Being deleted
questions.explanation: Data helps the game characters learn how to react in different situations.

questions.topic: Building an AI Game Step by Step
questions.question: What might happen if game creators SKIPPED the 'testing' step?
options: The game might not be fun or might not work properly when players try it
Nothing would change
The characters would instantly become perfect
Data would no longer be needed
questions.explanation: Skipping testing means problems with fun or function might not be caught before release.

questions.topic: Building an AI Game Step by Step
questions.question: What might happen if game creators SKIPPED the 'fixing mistakes' step?
options: Any errors in the game would stay, since nobody is checking or correcting them
The game would fix itself automatically without any help
The idea step would need to be repeated
Nothing bad would happen
questions.explanation: Without humans fixing mistakes, errors in the game would remain uncorrected.

questions.topic: Building an AI Game Step by Step
questions.question: Who writes the computer code that controls a game's characters and actions?
options: The game creators (humans)
The AI, on its own, before any humans are involved
Nobody — the code appears automatically
The players
questions.explanation: Human game creators write the code that controls the characters.

questions.topic: Building an AI Game Step by Step
questions.question: In this chapter's game example, only ONE of the five steps directly involves humans.
questions.explanation: All five steps (idea, code, data, test, fix) are done or led by human game creators.

questions.topic: Building an AI Game Step by Step
questions.question: Select ALL the steps in the 5-step process that show ongoing human OVERSIGHT (checking and improving) rather than just building.
options: Testing the game
Fixing mistakes and updating the game
Thinking of the idea
Writing the code
questions.explanation: Testing and fixing mistakes are the ongoing checking/improving steps, while idea and code are the initial building steps.

questions.topic: Building an AI Game Step by Step
questions.question: How many total steps are described for how humans lead AI game creation in this chapter?
options: Five
Two
Ten
Three
questions.explanation: There are five steps: idea, code, data, test, and fix.

questions.topic: Building an AI Game Step by Step
questions.question: Which of these best describes the relationship between the 5-step game process and the earlier 'Human Idea -> Instructions -> Training -> AI Output' chain?
options: The 5 steps are a detailed, real-life example of the same chain
They describe two completely unrelated processes
The 5-step process replaces the need for a human idea
The AI chain only applies to games, not other AI tools
questions.explanation: The game example illustrates the same idea/instructions/training/output pattern in more detail.

questions.topic: Building an AI Game Step by Step
questions.question: What is the purpose of 'giving the game lots of data' in this example?
options: So the characters can learn how to react in different situations
So the game looks nicer
So the code disappears
So testing is skipped
questions.explanation: Data teaches the game's characters how to react to different situations.

questions.topic: Building an AI Game Step by Step
questions.question: Game creators are the ones who test the game to make sure it is fun and works properly.
questions.explanation: Testing is done by the human game creators before the game is released.

questions.question: What mainly guides a HUMAN when making a decision?
options: Judgement, values, and understanding of the situation
Only patterns found in data
Random guessing
Nothing at all
questions.explanation: Humans use judgement, values and an understanding of context when they decide something.

questions.question: What mainly guides an AI when making a 'decision'?
options: Patterns and rules it learned from data
Personal feelings
Moral values
Random guessing, always
questions.explanation: An AI's 'decisions' come from patterns and rules it learned during training, not feelings or values.

questions.question: Which of these is true about AI decisions, according to this chapter?
options: AI follows patterns and rules learned from training, without truly understanding the situation
AI understands right and wrong exactly like a human
AI decisions are always better than human decisions
AI never uses any data to decide
questions.explanation: AI follows learned patterns and rules; it does not truly understand a situation the way a human does.

questions.question: Why can a human notice that a decision is unfair or unsafe in a way an AI might not?
options: Humans can use judgement, context, and values, while AI only follows learned patterns
AI always understands fairness better than humans
Humans never make mistakes
AI has feelings just like humans
questions.explanation: Human judgement and values allow people to notice things AI cannot, since AI only follows patterns.

questions.question: A human decision can be guided by values and understanding of consequences.
questions.explanation: Humans consider values and consequences when they decide something.

questions.question: An AI decision is guided by patterns learned from its training data and programmed rules.
questions.explanation: AI 'decisions' come from patterns in training data and the rules it was programmed with.

questions.question: A classmate says: 'AI thinks and feels exactly like a human when it decides something.' What is the problem with this statement?
options: AI follows patterns and rules; it does not truly think or feel like a human
This statement is completely correct
Humans do not use judgement at all
AI never uses data to decide anything
questions.explanation: AI does not have feelings or true understanding — it follows patterns learned from data.

questions.question: Because an AI can make fast decisions, it always understands WHY that decision matters, just like a human would.
questions.explanation: Speed does not mean understanding — AI can act quickly on patterns without grasping WHY a decision matters.

questions.question: In the video game example, why did game designers, not the AI, decide the villain's attack rules first?
options: Because only humans can imagine and set the boundaries and goals of the game before any pattern-following begins
Because AI always designs its own rules first
Because designers have nothing to do with attack patterns
Because rules are unnecessary for AI villains
questions.explanation: Humans must imagine and set the boundaries of what the AI is allowed to do before it can follow any patterns.

questions.question: Which decision requires understanding real-world consequences and values?
options: A teacher deciding what to teach a class
A screen displaying a number
A program repeating the same rule
None of these
questions.explanation: A teacher's choice involves judgement about what is best for students — a human decision.

questions.question: Select ALL the things that describe a HUMAN decision, according to this chapter's ideas.
options: Involves judgement and values
Considers the situation and consequences
Follows only patterns learned from past data
Can weigh what is fair or right
questions.explanation: Human decisions involve judgement, context and fairness. Following only learned patterns describes AI, not humans.

questions.question: Select ALL the things that describe an AI 'decision', according to this chapter's ideas.
options: Follows patterns and rules learned from training
Based on programmed instructions and data
Always includes moral judgement
Can act very quickly using what it learned
questions.explanation: AI decisions follow learned patterns and programmed rules, and can act quickly — but they do not include true moral judgement.

questions.question: Why do humans need to guide AI decisions instead of leaving AI fully on its own?
options: Because AI cannot use judgement or understand consequences the way humans can
Because AI is always slower than humans
Because humans cannot use computers
Because AI never uses any data
questions.explanation: Since AI lacks true judgement, humans must guide and check its decisions.

questions.question: Which statement best shows the DIFFERENCE between a human and an AI decision?
options: A human can ask 'is this fair?', while an AI can only follow the patterns and rules it was given
Both a human and an AI always agree
AI decisions never use any information
Human decisions never use judgement
questions.explanation: Humans can question fairness using judgement; AI simply follows the patterns and rules it learned.

questions.question: AI cannot use personal values or moral judgement the way a human can.
questions.explanation: AI follows learned patterns and rules; it does not have personal values or true moral judgement.

questions.question: Why might relying only on AI decisions (without human oversight) be risky, based on this chapter's theme?
options: Because AI might follow a pattern that is unfair or unsafe without realising it, since it lacks human judgement
Because AI is always 100% correct
Because humans are never involved in AI at all
Because AI decisions are never based on data
questions.explanation: Without human oversight, an AI's learned patterns might lead to unfair or unsafe outcomes that go unnoticed.

questions.question: What does the chapter suggest humans should do about AI's lack of judgement?
options: Guide, check and set boundaries on what AI can decide
Ignore the AI completely
Let AI make every decision alone
Remove all data from the AI
questions.explanation: Humans should guide and set boundaries since AI cannot judge situations the way people do.

questions.question: A human decision and an AI decision are made in exactly the same way.
questions.explanation: Human decisions use judgement and values; AI decisions follow learned patterns and rules — they are not the same.

questions.question: Which best explains why 'Setting the Boundaries of AI' (the chapter title) matters for decisions?
options: Because AI cannot judge right from wrong itself, humans must set limits on what it is allowed to decide
Because AI never makes any decisions
Because boundaries slow down human decisions only
Because AI decisions require no human input at all
questions.explanation: Since AI lacks true judgement, humans must set boundaries on what it can decide.

questions.question: Which of these best matches how an AI 'decides' something?
options: By matching the situation to patterns and rules it learned before
By feeling emotions about the choice
By asking a friend for advice
By guessing randomly every time
questions.explanation: AI matches situations to patterns and rules learned during training.

questions.question: Which of these five is the clearest example of a HUMAN actively guiding what happens, not an automatic AI/system action?
options: A teacher chooses lesson topics
Movie recommendations shown by an app
The photo app grouping dog pictures
The corridor lights turning on automatically
questions.explanation: A teacher actively deciding lesson topics is direct human guidance, unlike the automatic actions in the other options.

questions.question: Movie recommendations shown by an app are mostly the result of ____.
options: An AI/algorithm working automatically on patterns
A teacher deciding personally for each viewer
Random luck with no data involved
A person manually choosing every recommendation
questions.explanation: Movie recommendations are generated automatically by an algorithm using patterns in data.

options: The human-labelled images ARE the training data that lets the AI eventually produce a correct output (recognising a cat)
It has nothing to do with that chain
The chain only applies to games, not to image recognition
AI output always comes before any training in this story
questions.explanation: The human-labelled images are the training data step, leading to the AI's correct output.

questions.topic: Teaching AI to See Cats: The Google Story
questions.question: Which earlier chapter idea does 'humans choosing what data should be used' best match in the Google story?
options: Google's team choosing to use millions of human-labelled images (like ImageNet) to train the AI
The AI choosing its own images with no human input
The corridor lights turning on automatically
A platform suggesting toys
questions.explanation: Google's team chose to use human-labelled images to train the AI, matching the earlier 'humans choose data' idea.

questions.topic: Teaching AI to See Cats: The Google Story
questions.question: What kind of images did the human labellers work with, according to this story?
options: Millions of images
Only 10 images
No images at all
Only videos, no images
questions.explanation: The story describes human labellers looking at millions of images.

questions.topic: Teaching AI to See Cats: The Google Story
questions.question: A classmate says: 'Since the AI eventually recognised cats by itself, humans were not really needed.' What is wrong with this claim?
options: The AI could only recognise cats because thousands of humans first labelled the training images correctly
This claim is completely correct
The AI never needed any images to learn
ImageNet contains zero human-labelled images
questions.explanation: The AI's ability to recognise cats depended entirely on the human labelling work done beforehand.

questions.topic: Teaching AI to See Cats: The Google Story
questions.question: Select ALL the reasons the Google/ImageNet story is a good real-world example of 'Setting the Boundaries of AI'.
options: It shows humans deciding and preparing the exact data the AI is allowed to learn from
It shows AI teaching itself with absolutely no human input
It shows how much human effort goes into keeping AI's learning accurate and controlled
It proves AI needs no training data at all
questions.explanation: The story shows humans deciding the training data and putting in effort to keep AI's learning accurate — both support the chapter's theme.

questions.topic: Teaching AI to See Cats: The Google Story
questions.question: What does the word 'label' mean in this story (e.g., labelling an image 'This is a cat')?
options: Giving the image a correct name/tag so the AI can learn from it
Deleting the image
Making the image blurry
Changing the image's colour
questions.explanation: Labelling means giving an image a correct name/tag so the AI can learn from it.

questions.topic: Teaching AI to See Cats: The Google Story
questions.question: Why is ImageNet described as 'famous' in this chapter?
options: Because it is a very large, widely used dataset of 14 million human-labelled images for training AI
Because it only has 14 images
Because no AI has ever used it
Because it contains no labels at all
questions.explanation: ImageNet is famous for being a very large, widely used dataset of human-labelled images.

questions.topic: Teaching AI to See Cats: The Google Story
questions.question: Where can you learn more about the ImageNet dataset, according to the source given in this chapter?
options: image-net.org
a random search engine
a cooking website
a video game store
questions.explanation: The chapter's source lists image-net.org for more information about ImageNet.

questions.topic: Teaching AI to See Cats: The Google Story
questions.question: What real-world skill does the Google story help students practise, based on this chapter's sourcing?
options: Checking the source of information (like image-net.org) to see where a fact comes from
Ignoring where information comes from
Never questioning any fact
Assuming AI needs no sources at all
questions.explanation: Citing a source (image-net.org) models the skill of checking where information comes from.

questions.topic: Teaching AI to See Cats: The Google Story
questions.question: The Google story mentions a source about computers teaching themselves to spot cats on YouTube.
questions.explanation: The chapter cites an additional source about Google computers learning to identify cats on YouTube.

questions.topic: Teaching AI to See Cats: The Google Story
questions.question: Which best summarises the MAIN lesson of the Google/ImageNet story for this chapter?
options: Massive human effort (labelling data) is often needed behind the scenes before an AI can 'learn' something as simple as recognising a cat
AI recognised cats instantly with zero data or human help
Cats cannot be recognised by any AI, ever
This story has nothing to do with AI training
questions.explanation: The main lesson is that a huge amount of human effort is needed behind the scenes to train an AI.

questions.topic: Teaching AI to See Cats: The Google Story
questions.question: In this story, which of these was NOT one of the three example labels given?
options: 'This is a bird'
'This is a cat'
'This is a dog'
'This is a car'
questions.explanation: The three example labels given were cat, dog and car — not bird.

questions.topic: Teaching AI to See Cats: The Google Story
questions.question: This chapter's Google story proves that AI can learn to recognise objects with no human-provided data at all.
questions.explanation: The story actually shows the opposite — the AI needed 10,000 human labellers and millions of labelled images to learn.

questions.topic: Teaching AI to See Cats: The Google Story
questions.question: What does this story suggest about the amount of human effort that can go into training an AI?
options: It can be enormous — Google hired 10,000 people just for labelling
It is always zero
It only takes one person a few minutes
AI never needs any human effort
questions.explanation: The story shows an enormous amount of human effort (10,000 people) was needed for labelling alone.

questions.topic: Teaching AI to See Cats: The Google Story
questions.question: How does the Google story support the idea that 'choosing what data should be used' is a HUMAN job (from earlier in the chapter)?
options: Google's team specifically chose and prepared millions of human-labelled images for training, rather than letting the AI pick its own data
The AI chose its own images with no human decision at all
This story shows data does not matter for AI
This story is about game testing, not data
questions.explanation: Google's team chose and prepared the training data themselves, confirming this is a human job.

questions.topic: Teaching AI to See Cats: The Google Story
questions.question: What is the overall theme connecting the Google/ImageNet story to the rest of this chapter?
options: Humans guide, prepare, and set the boundaries for how AI learns and works
AI works completely independently of any human effort
Only games use AI, not image recognition
Data has nothing to do with how AI learns
questions.explanation: The Google story reinforces the chapter's overall theme that humans guide and set the boundaries of how AI learns and works.
